ML_TIP_PREPARE_TEXT: You notice the world with your eyes and ears, a robot does that with sensors. Pick sensors that can actually notice the difference between your classes: a distance sensor can tell "wall ahead" from "free path", but not red from blue.
ML_TIP_COLLECT_TEXT: Every moment you hold a key, the robot saves a flashcard: what its sensors notice, plus the right answer. Vary your examples (distance, angle, light) and give every class about the same number of cards, otherwise the brain just guesses the biggest pile.
ML_TIP_TRAIN_TEXT: The brain goes through all flashcards and adjusts itself a little every time it gets one wrong. One pass through the whole stack is called an epoch. Some cards are kept apart for an exam later, so we can check it really learned instead of memorising the answers.
ML_TIP_RESULT_TEXT: The brain was tested with flashcards it never studied. If it mixes up two classes, record more (and more varied) examples of both and train again. That's how real AI engineers improve their models too!

ML_SENSOR_ANALOG_DESCRIPTION: Something that goes from low to high, like a light sensor or a knob.
ML_SENSOR_ULTRASONIC_DESCRIPTION: Measures distance with sound, like a bat.
ML_SENSOR_TOF_DESCRIPTION: Measures distance with an invisible laser.
ML_SENSOR_LIDAR_DESCRIPTION: Sees distances in an 8×8 grid, like a tiny low-resolution camera.

TEACHABLE_MACHINE_TIP_RECORD_TEXT: Every recording is a flashcard with a sound and its name. Record each sound in different ways: louder, softer, closer and further away.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_BACKGROUND_HINT: Record the room as it normally sounds, so the model knows when nothing special is happening.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_TIP_TRAIN_TEXT: The model studies your flashcards over and over. It also makes slightly changed copies, like hearing the same word in a different room, so it learns the sound and not the recording.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_TRAINING_LOSS_DESC: This line goes down as the model learns from its mistakes.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_FINAL_ACCURACY_DESC: How often the model recognised the right sound at the end of studying.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_EPOCHS_HINT: How many times the model goes through all samples.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_LEARNING_RATE_HINT: How big the steps are the model takes when it learns. Too big and it overshoots, too small and it learns slowly.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_BATCH_SIZE_HINT: How many samples the model looks at before it adjusts itself.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_L2_REGULARIZATION_HINT: Keeps the model simple, so it doesn't memorise your recordings.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_VARIATIONS_PER_SAMPLE_: How many slightly changed copies are made of every recording.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_LAYER_BACKGROUND_NOISE: Mixes background noise into your recordings, so the model also works in a noisy room.
TEACHABLE_MACHINE_TIP_TEST_TEXT: Make your sounds and watch the bars. Does it confuse two sounds? Record more varied samples of both and train again.
